subject: image cropping based on spatial positioning

messages.author: 3345fe7ecebfb837
messages.subject: image cropping based on spatial positioning
parts:
Hello,

I have a situation that is a bit different from the tutorial examples. The field I'm working on has several thousand ~1m x 1m research plots. This makes any FIELDimageR functions that require manual selection, like fieldShape(), difficult to perform precisely due to the small image window and inability to zoom in rstudio.

My current workaround is to use an image editor (gimp) to rotate and crop my raw images while zoomed in to precisely select the field corners. These rotated/cropped images can then be processed automatically using the fieldShape() extent = TRUE option. (instructs fieldShape() to use the entire image and skip manual corner selection) This works well for basic processing like canopy percentage. However, gimp is not geotiff-aware, so it does not export spatial information after rotating/cropping, crippling it's usefulness.

Moving forward, I'm considering pre-processing steps similar to those above. Avoiding manual selections in FIELDimageR while retaining spatial information in the rotated/cropped TIFs is the goal. Ideally I'd automate as much of the processing as possible for consistency (and speed!) between the time-series images I have. This seems feasible, but I have very limited experience with geotiff files and am not sure if there is a way to get spatial coordinates from field corners in an image and if those coordinates can be used for cropping. If anyone has experience doing this, I'd like to hear more about your process.

Thanks,
Brian

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: image cropping based on spatial positioning
parts:
Hi Brian,

 

Thanks for sharing your experience and thoughts with us. For the next version of FIELDimageR, I have some ideas to improve this step… I will let you know when it is done.

 

In the meantime, there are some great solutions. Do you know the package UAStools (https://github.com/andersst91/UAStools)? This package allows using only the coordinate information from each corner to build the plot shapefile, check this tutorial from Steven L. Anderson https://github.com/andersst91/UAStools/wiki/plotshpcreate.R. Also, there is a great workshop video that combines UAStools and FIELDimageR presented by Alper Adak. Here is the link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-xmC8qCt7k.

 

Another possibility is to use QGIS to build your plot shapefile. Here is a great workshop presented by Diego Gris https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wrPPKSniXW0.

 

In case you have experience with python, Tyler Nigon presented this super cool tool to make plot shapefiles as well. Check this workshop link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k26YPRY4qdk

 

Hope one of these solutions helps you… Please, let us know if it works.

 

All the best,

Filipe

parts:
Hi Filipe,

Good to hear you have plans to improve this aspect of FIELDimageR, I will look forward to testing the modifications when available. Until then, I will test the suggestions you provided. I am currently pushing the recommended maximum mosaic size, so it may be best for me to crop images prior to FIELDimageR processing, just to keep the input mosaic file size as low as possible.

Thanks again,
Brian
